headline: Amazon's Zoox wins first US approval for driverless robotaxis
summary:
STORY: :: Archive

What if your next driverless taxi had no steering wheel? That may soon become a reality.

Amazon-owned Zoox has won the first U.S. approval for commercial deployment of a robotaxi built without traditional human controls.

The approval came from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, or NHTSA...

allowing the company to begin charging for rides in Las Vegas once it completes state requirements.

Here's NHTSA administrator Jonathan Morrison.

"Since our standards get into performance requirements for specific aspects such as braking performance, they provided information and we received public comment, and we made that determination that their vehicle as equipped, can meet all of those requirements and in fact, exceed those."

The vehicle looks very different from a conventional car.

It's an electric, carriage-style robotaxi with two rows of inward-facing seats and a top speed of 75 miles per hour.

Federal officials say Zoox can deploy up to 2,500 vehicles in each of the next two years.

The move comes as companies including Alphabet's Waymo and Elon Musk's Tesla race to expand driverless ride-hailing services across the U.S.

The green light comes with added oversight.

U.S. regulators say the firm must report issues including crashes and inappropriate stops.

Authorities also retain the power to revoke the exemption if major safety concerns emerge.

headline: Amazon soars as cloud revenue surge allays fears over ballooning AI bets
summary: Amazon shares surged 13% premarket on Friday after the tech giant's solid cloud sales growth reinforced investor confidence in its massive AI ‌bets and quashed any concerns about the company trailing its Big Tech rivals in the ‌AI race.  The e-commerce and cloud titan posted its strongest cloud growth in over four years, indicating a fresh wave of demand that justifies ​its 10% increase in planned capital spending for 2026 to $220 billion.  Amazon's results come as a resounding sign to Wall Street that some of Big Tech's AI investments are already generating measurable returns.
